Package dev.opencollab.paletter.vanilla

Class BedrockBlockType

java.lang.Object
dev.opencollab.paletter.vanilla.BedrockBlockType
public final class BedrockBlockType extends Object
A Bedrock block type: an identifier with its state properties. Vanilla types are the constants of BedrockBlocks; a CustomBlock has one too (CustomBlock.type()), so both are used alike: 

 BedrockBlockState door = BedrockBlocks.WOODEN_DOOR.state()
     .with(BedrockStates.CARDINAL_DIRECTION, CardinalDirection.NORTH)
     .with(BedrockStates.OPEN_BIT, true)
     .build();
 int runtimeId = palette.runtimeId(door);
Referencing a type loads nothing; its states are resolved against the newest data of Paletter.bundled() on first use. A vanilla constant the newest bundled release does not have (deprecated because Bedrock removed the block, or a @SincePreview block) is not available, but has states of its own, like an item constant: a preview block those of the preview, written into the constant when it was generated (no preview data is loaded for them), a removed block one state without properties. A palette whose newest version has the block (a preview block in a Paletter with previews) sends the block itself; any other palette resolves its states through its Fallbacks, minecraft:unknown by default.

Equality: like its states (see BedrockBlockState), equals always works, and == works for the vanilla constants, the preview's blocks among them, and for the type a registered CustomBlock owns. Not in a Paletter with previews, for the blocks of the release the preview changed: those have types of their own, equal to the constant if the states are the same.

Since:
1.0.0

    • custom

      @Internal public static @NonNull BedrockBlockType custom(@NonNull String identifier, @NonNull List<BlockProperty<?>> properties, @NonNull Map<String,Object> defaultStates)
      Internal: plumbing of CustomBlock, which creates its type once and owns it: use CustomBlock.type().
      Parameters:
      identifier - the block identifier
      properties - the state properties, in declaration order (CustomBlock.stateProperties())
      defaultStates - the values of the default state; properties not listed use their first value
      Returns:
      a new custom type. Loads no data

    • fromIdentifier

      @Internal public static @NonNull BedrockBlockType fromIdentifier(@NonNull String identifier)
      Internal: the key of an identifier: the vanilla constant if the identifier (after renames) is a vanilla block of the newest bundled data or has a generated constant, else a custom type known by its identifier only (no states). Such types are not interned: equal for equal identifiers, not identical, so compare them with equals, and unknown identifiers never accumulate. Use byIdentifier(String). The type of a CustomBlock is CustomBlock.type(). Loads the data.
      Parameters:
      identifier - a block identifier
      Returns:
      the type of the identifier

    • byIdentifier

      public static @Nullable BedrockBlockType byIdentifier(@NonNull String identifier)
      Finds the vanilla type of an identifier, without making a type for an unknown identifier. The identifier is first mapped through the renames of the bundled data, so the name an older version gave a block finds its type. Loads the data.
      Parameters:
      identifier - a block identifier
      Returns:
      the vanilla constant, or null if the identifier (after renames) is not a block of the newest bundled data and has no generated constant
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if the identifier is null
      Since:
      1.0.0
